_proposal: A PROPOSAL for the owner's Q2, not a decision. Eight prompts, fixed, so the v1-vs-v2 comparison measures the prompt and the vocabulary rather than taste. Replace any or all of them: the classes matter more than the subjects.

_classes.repetition: Has something that appears several times, so `defs` + `ref` can show their worth. v2 should use fewer written entries AND spend the saved budget on detail; if it does neither, the vocabulary is not earning.
_classes.silhouette: Wants a profile no primitive has. Reserved for G3's extrude/lathe — these should look CONSTRAINED under both v1 and v2, which is the control that proves G3 was the missing piece rather than the prompt.
_classes.box-dominant: Almost no curved masses. The radius/diameter bug (note 197) halved every sphere, cylinder, cone and torus, so a box-dominant subject is the one that was NOT affected. Without it, the before/after cannot separate 'v2 is better' from 'the curves are no longer half size'.
_classes.unsuited: Beyond any parts list — organic, jointed, or needing hundreds of elements. Included deliberately so the table has a floor. If v2 scores well here something is wrong with the measurement, not right with v2.

prompts.text: a hand cart with four spoked wheels and a plank bed
prompts.why: The worked example's own subject. If the prompt teaches `defs` at all, this is where it shows.

prompts.text: a ruined colonnade, eight fluted columns on a stepped plinth
prompts.why: Repetition with variation — the columns should differ in placement, not in piece. Curve-dominant, so note 197 hit it hardest.

prompts.text: a brass chandelier with six arms, each holding a lit candle
prompts.why: Repetition plus emissive restraint; six arms is the case where writing it out by hand eats the budget.

prompts.text: a brutalist concrete bench, two slabs and a cantilever
prompts.why: THE CONTROL for note 197: almost no curved parts, so it rendered correctly before the prompt fix. Its score should move least.

prompts.text: a tall ceramic vase with a flared lip and a narrow waist
prompts.why: A lathe profile and nothing else. Should stay visibly approximate until G3.

prompts.text: a five-pointed star lantern glowing from inside
prompts.why: An extruded polygon. A five-pointed star is the shape six primitives cannot fake.

prompts.text: a seated human figure, hands on knees
prompts.why: The floor. Jointed and organic; a parts list should read as a mannequin at best.

prompts.text: an oak tree in full summer leaf
prompts.why: The other floor. Foliage needs hundreds of elements; 28 leaf parts cannot.
